pass_rule: all core questions substantially correct in the learner's own words; stretch questions inform the grade, not the gate

questions.prompt: Sketch how linkcheck works end to end: where do goroutines, channels, and context each appear, and why does none of them show up in Check's signature?
expected_points: jobs flow through a closed, buffered channel of indexes to a fixed pool of worker goroutines
a WaitGroup joins the workers; results land by index so order is preserved
the context flows from main (signal.NotifyContext) through Check into every request
Check's signature stays synchronous (slice in, slice out) so callers and tests never touch the concurrency

questions.prompt: Why bound the pool at all instead of one goroutine per URL, and what mechanism enforces the bound in your implementation?
expected_points: unbounded fan-out can overwhelm the target and exhaust local resources (sockets, file descriptors, memory)
exactly Concurrency worker goroutines pull from the jobs channel, so at most that many requests are in flight
closing the jobs channel is the shutdown signal that ends each worker's range loop

questions.prompt: Each request derives its own context.WithTimeout from Check's context. Why per request rather than one deadline around the whole run, and why does Ctrl-C still cut a request short?
expected_points: a shared deadline makes URLs late in the list inherit a nearly spent budget after one slow target
per-request derivation gives every URL the same fresh budget
child contexts inherit cancellation, so canceling the parent aborts the request before its own deadline
defer cancel() releases the timer even on success

questions.prompt: Walk through what happens between pressing Ctrl-C and seeing the summary line, and what 'partial results' means for the report.
expected_points: signal.NotifyContext cancels the run context on SIGINT
in-flight requests abort because http.Client.Do honors the request context, returning errors wrapping context.Canceled
workers keep draining jobs but record ctx.Err() instead of making new requests
Check still returns one Result per URL, so the report accounts for every URL including the canceled ones

questions.prompt: The tests never sleep and never touch the real network, yet they verify 'at most 3 requests in flight' and 'no new requests after cancel'. How? And what did the race detector add?
expected_points: httptest servers on 127.0.0.1 with gate handlers: signal arrival on one channel, block on a release channel, so the test holds the pool in a known state
an in-flight counter in the handler records the maximum observed concurrency; the cancel test counts server hits
watchdog time.After selects convert would-be hangs into readable failures without making correct code flaky
-race reports unsynchronized access pairs (e.g. appending to a shared slice) even when tests pass; indexed writes plus wg.Wait stay silent because they are properly ordered

questions.prompt: A reviewer asks: 'Why write results by index instead of sending them over a channel or guarding a slice with a mutex? And how would you pick a default for -c?' Defend your choices.
expected_points: each index has exactly one writer and wg.Wait publishes the writes, so indexed assignment is race-free without locks and keeps input order
a results channel wins when results must stream out as they complete or the count is unknown; a mutex+append loses order for no benefit here
pool size trades throughput against pressure on targets and local limits; the workload is I/O-bound so it need not match GOMAXPROCS, and the right default is modest with a flag to tune
